title: Quiz: Decision Trees and Random Forests

questions.text: At a node with 80 non-churners and 20 churners (n=100), what is the Gini impurity?
In a random forest with p = 9 predictor variables, how many features are randomly considered at each split (default for classification)?
questions.explanation: For classification, the default in randomForest is mtry = floor(√p). With p = 9, mtry = floor(√9) = floor(3) = 3.

questions.text: What is the Out-of-Bag (OOB) error in a random forest?
options: The error on the training set for each tree
The error computed on the ~37% of observations not included in each tree's bootstrap sample
The error on a separate held-out test set
The cross-validation error averaged across k folds
questions.explanation: Each bootstrap sample draws n rows with replacement, leaving ~37% of observations out. For each tree, these OOB observations are used to evaluate that tree's predictions. Averaging OOB predictions across all trees gives the OOB error — a nearly unbiased test error estimate without requiring a separate test set.

questions.text: Precision = TP / (TP + FP). In a fraud detection context, what does low precision mean?
options: The model misses many genuine fraud cases
The model raises many false alarms — many flagged cases are not actually fraudulent
The model's predictions are unstable across different test sets
The model is overfitting the training data
questions.explanation: Precision = proportion of flagged cases that are genuinely positive. Low precision means many of the model's 'fraud' predictions are actually legitimate claims — false positives. This wastes investigators' time. High recall (low FN rate) is the complement concern.

questions.text: A single decision tree is a high-variance model, meaning small changes in the training data can lead to very different tree structures.
questions.explanation: Decision trees are greedy and deterministic: the first split is chosen based on all training data, and a different training sample can produce a completely different first split. This high variance is why bagging (random forests) is so effective — averaging many unstable estimators reduces variance dramatically.

questions.text: ROC-AUC of 0.5 for a binary classifier means:
options: The model performs no better than random guessing
The model correctly classifies all cases but one
questions.explanation: ROC-AUC = 0.5 corresponds to the diagonal line in ROC space — the curve of a classifier that randomly assigns class probabilities. Any model with AUC = 0.5 provides no discriminative power beyond chance. AUC = 1.0 is a perfect classifier; AUC > 0.7 is generally considered useful.
